page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running on the Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. The system provides 64 GB of system memory, matching an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. In addition, the instance integrates a dedicated 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. No discrete GPUs are included.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance, highlighted by a PassMark memory score of 2,935.53 placing it within the top 25% of measured configurations. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests achieve 169.31 GB/sec for reads and 68.70 GB/sec for writes. Compute performance across Stress-ng and Geekbench yields scores in the middle 50% range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,652.00 and Stress-ng multi-core throughput of 13,642.44. In-memory data store performance reached 16.62 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, hardware cryptographic tests under PassMark registered lower comparative throughput in the bottom 25%, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing exhibited limited CPU inference throughput.

By combining high memory density with high-speed local NVMe scratch storage on dedicated Arm-based silicon, the r8gd.2xlarge delivers solid resource efficiency for workloads that require fast temporary I/O alongside extensive RAM pools. Key suitable workloads include in-memory databases like Redis, transactional databases needing rapid write-ahead caching, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with dedicated physical cores, the instance provides 64 GB of system memory, achieving an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a 4 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark data reflects notable memory performance, where PassMark memory metrics rank in the top quartile and uncached read bandwidth reaches 169.31 GB/sec. Standard compute benchmarks such as Geekbench and Stress-ng reflect steady average throughput across general processing, while cryptographic hashing shows lower relative efficiency. With its combination of dedicated Arm compute cores, dense memory capacity, and low-latency local NVMe scratch storage, the r8gd.2xlarge is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory key-value databases, distributed caching clusters, and transactional database environments.
